source: Vinokurova N. Lexical Categories and Argument Structure: A Study with Reference to Sakha. Utrecht, 2005. (LOT Dissertation Series, no. 103)
topic: Double accusative and the part-whole relationship
notes: One more double accusative context has been introduced in 3.1.2.3. It involves an inalienable possessive DP in the object position marked with accusative case (98a). Case marking is reflected on the head of the DP – the possessed noun. However, the possessor can also be marked accusative as (98b) indicates. (99a) shows that what is involved is not inalienability per se but rather the part-whole relationship as can also be witnessed from (99b) and (99c).
